A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same YOLO-RD study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection and segmentation experiments on COCO, classification experiments on CIFAR-100, VOC transfer experiments, and ablation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original task and ablation results and additionally reports latency measurements, YOLOv7-x comparison results, and dictionary-distribution visualizations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same retriever, normalization, dictionary initialization, training, and compression procedures. The added soft-label explanation retains the existing contrastive loss. Revised parameter counts do not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO detection/segmentation, CIFAR-100 classification, and VOC transfer learning, with the same COCO and ImageNet-21k text sources for initialization. The added latency and dictionary analyses introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds an explicit YOLOv7-x comparison, reporting 71.3M parameters and 51.29 AP; v1 only mentions this larger model narratively. The existing detector comparisons and KD, YOLO-World, and RALF comparator set remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds latency evaluation in milliseconds per batch, using one Nvidia 3090, batch size 32, COCO validation data, and no external acceleration tools (Section 4.1). Faster R-CNN training is qualified as a maximum of 120 epochs rather than 120 epochs. These descriptions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.7 and Figures 12–13 examine initial VM, VLM, and LLM dictionary distributions through 2D/3D t-SNE. V1's learning curves and convergence analysis in Figure 10 and A.3 are removed. Existing construction, retriever-fusion, dictionary-freezing, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or performance error bars. The added t-SNE plots depict feature distributions rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported scores receive limited revisions: YOLOv7/VLM AP changes from 51.72 to 51.75 in Table 1, and YOLO-World mAP/AP50 changes from 50.81/67.56 to 51.00/67.70 in Table 3. Latency, baseline entries, and t-SNE findings are added; convergence curves are removed. Some revisions are inconsistent across tables: v2 Table 1 reports 25.5M parameters for YOLOv9 VM/VLM, while Table 6 retains 25.8M.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, compression objective, convolution-equivalence derivations, and gradient-update reasoning are retained. Numbering the previously unnumbered compression loss and moving v1 Appendix A.7 to v2 A.8 do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: efficient external-knowledge integration, improvements across vision tasks and architectures, and over 3% detection improvement with under 1% additional parameters. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V1 A.3's separate interpretation that explicit knowledge accelerates early learning is removed with the learning curves, although the VOC convergence discussion remains. V2 A.7 connects its t-SNE observations to the existing richer-VLM-knowledge explanation. No new limitations are stated.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-release link in the abstract and hardware, batch-size, and acceleration details for latency measurement. Section 4.1 revises reported YOLOv7 training time from three days to two while retaining 300 epochs. The underlying training pseudocode and default hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to YOLO, dictionary learning, and retrieval augmentation remain the same. Changes such as updating RT-DETR's 2023 citation to its 2024 conference reference are bibliographic updates rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording and bibliographic edits, adds the conference header, promotes the conclusion from Section 4.5 to Section 5, and inserts an appendix subsection with corresponding renumbering. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to show the detection pipeline and preprocessing. Table 1 replaces its dictionary-size column with latency, and Table 6 gains baseline rows. V1 Figure 10 is removed and v2 Figures 12–13 are added; the existing qualitative examples are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The latency measurements and stated protocol, explicit YOLOv7-x comparison, code-release link, and clearer Figure 2 provide a limited net improvement in evaluating efficiency and understanding the implementation. These gains are tempered by removal of the convergence curves and numerical inconsistencies introduced between Tables 1 and 6, including the YOLOv9 parameter counts.
